en: to reduce; to cut down on

examples.en: To turn down the sound
I cut down on coffee this month.
I've cut back on how much rice I eat at dinner.

examples.ko: TV 소리가 너무 커요. 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: The TV is too loud. Please turn it down.
I want to cut down on salt. The soup is salty.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 너무 커요. 크기를 줄여요.
examples.en: This photo is too big. I'll make it smaller.

explain: 줄이다는 내가 줄이는 거예요. 저절로 작아지면 “줄다”예요: 옷이 줄었어요.

dict_examples.en: We downsized our home and moved.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I altered Mother's clothes smaller and dressed my younger sibling in them.

explain_en: 줄이다 is something you do on purpose. When it shrinks by itself, use 줄다: 옷이 줄었어요 (“The clothes shrank”).

gh: formal; make amounts or levels drop

p.n: 감소시키다 is for abstract amounts, not turning down volume.

en: to stand (something) up; to stop (a car)

examples.en: To stop the car
Stand the book up on the desk.
Please stop the car here.
There's no parking lot. I park the car by the roadside.
I hailed a taxi in front of the convenience store.
The child stacks the blocks up high.

explain: 세우다는 ‘서다’의 짝이에요. 버스가 서요 → 버스를 세워요. 내가 하면 ‘세우다’, 저절로 되면 ‘서다’예요.

phrases.nuance_en: used when you decide on a plan or goal and set it down

dict_examples.en: Park a car in front of the house.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나가는 사람을 불러 세워 김밥을 사다 달라고 부탁했다.
dict_examples.en: I called over someone who was leaving and asked them to buy some gimbap.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 기계를 한번 세우면 재가동하는 데 여러모로 손실이 크다.
dict_examples.en: Once you stop a machine, restarting it causes considerable losses in many ways.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 세우다 is the “make it happen” partner of 서다. The bus stops: 버스가 서요. You stop the bus: 버스를 세워요.

examples.en: Melt the butter.
I thawed the frozen meat in water.
I melted chocolate and spread it on the cake.

examples.ko: 추워서 손을 녹이려고 따뜻한 차를 마셔요.
examples.en: It's cold, so I drink hot tea to warm my hands.
You can melt ice with a microwave.

explain: ‘녹다’는 저절로 녹는 거고, ‘녹이다’는 열을 써서 일부러 녹게 하는 거예요. 추운 날 ‘손을 녹이다’, ‘몸을 녹이다’처럼 차가워진 몸을 따뜻하게 할 때도 많이 써요. 반대말은 ‘얼리다’예요.

phrases.example: 아기의 웃음이 무뚝뚝한 할아버지의 마음을 녹였어요.
phrases.en: The baby's smile melted the gruff grandfather's heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차갑거나 굳은 마음을 부드럽고 따뜻하게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: means making a cold or hardened heart soft and warm
phrases.en_equiv: The baby's smile melted the gruff grandfather's heart.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To melt sugar and make it like taffy.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: It is hot enough to melt asphalt.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To eat candy by letting it melt in your mouth.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: '녹다' is melting by itself; '녹이다' is melting something on purpose with heat. On cold days it's also used for warming up, as in '손을 녹이다' or '몸을 녹이다'. The opposite is '얼리다' (to freeze).

en: to move emotionally; to touch; to impress

examples.en: That song moved everyone.
I want to move my parents with a letter.
It is a film that moves people.
A small gift touches a friend.
What touched the teacher was the student's effort.

examples.ko: 말만으로는 그 사람을 감동시킬 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't move that person with words alone.

explain: 느끼게 하는 쪽이 주어예요. 느끼는 사람이 주어이면 '감동받다'를 써요. '노래가 나를 감동시켰어요'와 '나는 노래에 감동받았어요'를 비교해 보세요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 저에게 큰 감동을 줬어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감동시키다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 더 자연스럽게 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '감동시키다' and often sounds more natural.

phrases.en: I was moved after reading my friend's letter.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the person who feels the emotion is the subject.

explain_en: The subject is whoever causes the feeling. If the person who feels it is the subject, use '감동받다'. Compare '노래가 나를 감동시켰어요' with '나는 노래에 감동받았어요'.

en: to show around; to let someone see

examples.en: I showed my friend around Seoul.
I want to take my child to see the zoo.

examples.ko: 외국 친구에게 부산을 구경시켜서 하루가 금방 갔어요.
examples.en: I showed my foreign friend around Busan, and the day flew by.
It is time to show the guests around the factory.
Next time, there are many places I can show you.
I showed my family around my office and they all liked it.

explain: '구경하다'는 내가 보는 것이고 '구경시키다'는 다른 사람이 볼 수 있게 해 주는 거예요. 보통 '구경시켜 주다', '구경시켜 드리다'로 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '보여 주다'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I showed my younger sibling around our school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족처럼 편한 사람에게 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing someone around, such as friends or family.

phrases.en: I showed my parents my room.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 드리다 when the person is older or higher in status.

phrases.en: I showed my friend our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구경시키다'보다 짧고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 구경시키다 and more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: 구경하다 is when you look around yourself, while 구경시키다 is letting someone else look around. It usually appears as 구경시켜 주다 or 구경시켜 드리다. 보여 주다 is also a common alternative.

en: to make remember; to make recall

examples.en: The teacher made a song to help us remember the words.
This ad makes you remember the brand name.
I got my child to memorize our home address.

examples.ko: 부모님은 어릴 때부터 제 이름과 전화번호를 기억시키셨어요.
examples.en: My parents made me remember my name and phone number from when I was little.
We need to make the staff remember the safety rules.

examples.ko: 시험 날짜를 학생들에게 기억시키는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to make students remember the exam date.

explain: 다른 사람이 기억하게 만든다는 말이에요. 비슷한 상황에서 한국 사람들은 '알려 주다', '상기시키다', '외우게 하다'도 써요. '기억하다'가 내가 기억하는 것이라면 이 말은 상대를 향해요.

phrases.en: I help people remember words with a song.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more natural in daily speech than '기억시키다'.

phrases.en: I said my name many times so they'd remember it.
phrases.nuance_en: A common connecting form for stating a purpose.

phrases.example: 저는 사람들에게 제 이름을 기억시키지 못했어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't make people remember my name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 기억하게 하는 데 실패했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you failed to make others remember.

explain_en: It means causing another person to remember something. In similar situations Koreans also use '알려 주다' (let someone know), '상기시키다' (remind) and '외우게 하다' (make someone memorize). '기억하다' is what you do yourself, while 기억시키다 is directed at someone else.

en: to frighten; to scare; to shock

examples.ko: 생일에 몰래 준비해서 엄마를 놀래 줬어요.
examples.en: I secretly prepared something on her birthday and surprised my mom.
Do not startle the child with a loud voice.
I am going to surprise my husband with a surprise party.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 갑자기 소리를 질러서 저를 놀랬어요.
examples.en: He suddenly shouted from behind and startled me.
I did not mean to scare you, sorry.
I even scared my younger sibling with a scary mask.

explain: '놀라다'는 내가 놀라는 것이고, '놀래다'는 다른 사람을 놀라게 하는 것이에요: '친구를 놀래다'. 내가 놀랐을 때는 '놀랐어요'예요. 입말에서 '놀래키다'라고도 하지만 표준어는 '놀래다'예요.

phrases.example: 남편을 놀래 주고 싶어서 케이크를 준비했어요.
phrases.en: I wanted to surprise my husband, so I prepared a cake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깜짝 선물처럼 즐겁게 놀라게 하고 싶을 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used when you want to surprise someone in a fun way.

phrases.example: 큰 소리로 사람을 놀라게 하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't startle people with a loud noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀래다'와 뜻이 같고, 더 널리 쓰이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 놀래다, and more widely used.

phrases.example: 숨어 있다가 친구를 깜짝 놀래 줬어요.
phrases.en: I hid and then gave my friend a big scare.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깜짝'을 붙이면 갑자기 놀라게 한다는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 깜짝 stresses the sudden surprise.

explain_en: '놀라다' is when you are startled yourself; 'nollaeda' is when you startle someone else, as in '친구를 놀래다'. When you are the one startled, say '놀랐어요'. In speech you may hear '놀래키다', but the standard word is '놀래다'.

examples.ko: 유아 전용 놀이방이 있는 식당이라 아기 손님이 많이 와요.
examples.en: It's a restaurant with a play room for little kids, so many baby customers come.
I leave my child at the daycare and go to work.
At the daycare, he plays with blocks with his friends.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 놀이방은 오후 일곱 시까지 열어요.
examples.en: The daycare in our neighborhood is open until seven in the evening.

examples.ko: 놀이방 선생님이 아이를 잘 돌봐 주세요.
examples.en: The daycare teacher takes good care of the child.

examples.ko: 거실 한쪽에 아이 놀이방을 따로 만들었어요.
examples.en: We made a separate play room for the child in one corner of the living room.

explain: 아이를 돌봐 주는 시설을 말하기도 하고, 식당이나 집 안에 아이가 놀 수 있게 만든 공간을 말하기도 해요. 시설을 말할 때는 요즘 보통 '어린이집'이라고 불러요. 뜻이 두 가지라서 문장에서 시설인지 공간인지 구분해서 읽어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 시설을 말할 때 요즘 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common word these days for the childcare facility.

phrases.en: I leave my child at the daycare while I work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이를 돌봐 주는 시설이라는 뜻으로 쓸 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when you mean the facility that looks after children.
phrases.en_equiv: to leave a child at daycare

phrases.en: It's convenient to go to a restaurant that has a play area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이때는 시설이 아니라 아이가 노는 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it means a play space, not a childcare facility.

explain_en: It can mean a facility that looks after children, or a space in a restaurant or home made for kids to play. For the facility, people now usually call it '어린이집'. Since it has two meanings, check from the sentence whether it is a facility or a space.
